summary:
AuroraX – Live Space Weather Intelligence

AuroraX is an interactive space-weather monitoring platform developed by Team AuroraX for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It is designed to make real-time solar activity and space-weather information accessible through a simple, informative and interactive dashboard.

The platform connects with NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) and NASA's DONKI API to collect and display important information about solar wind, magnetic fields, X-ray activity, geomagnetic storms and solar events.

Core Features

1. Live Solar Telemetry: Displays the latest solar wind, magnetic field and X-ray measurements through interactive charts covering the last six hours.

2. Space-Weather Impacts: Explains the potential effects of solar activity using NOAA's geomagnetic storm (G) and radio blackout (R) scales.

3. Aurora Visibility Estimator: Allows users to enter geographical coordinates or use their location to estimate geomagnetic latitude and determine whether aurora visibility conditions are favourable.

Technology Used

- HTML
- CSS
- JavaScript
- Netlify Functions
- NASA DONKI API


Project Mission

AuroraX aims to bridge the gap between complex scientific space-weather data and public understanding. By combining real-time monitoring, interactive visualisations and aurora estimation, it helps users explore solar activity and understand its potential influence on Earth's environment and technological systems.
details:
AuroraX – Reading the Sun, Understanding Earth 1. What does the project do and how does it work? AuroraX is an interactive space-weather monitoring platform designed to make real-time solar activity and its effects on Earth easier to understand. The platform collects scientific data from NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) and NASA's DONKI API. It processes and presents this information through an interactive dashboard, allowing users to monitor solar wind speed, magnetic field conditions, X-ray activity and geomagnetic conditions. AuroraX includes four major sections: - Telemetry: Displays real-time solar wind, magnetic field and X-ray measurements, including six-hour data visualisations. - Impacts: Explains potential effects of space weather using NOAA's geomagnetic storm (G) and radio blackout (R) scales. - Aurora Estimator: Allows users to enter geographical coordinates or share their location to estimate geomagnetic latitude and compare the Kp level required for aurora visibility with current conditions. - Events and Alerts: Displays official NOAA space-weather alerts, NASA-recorded solar flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs) from the last 14 days. Users can also download telemetry information in CSV format for further analysis. 2. What benefits does it have? AuroraX makes complex scientific information more accessible and understandable. Its major benefits include: - Helps users monitor solar activity and changing space-weather conditions. - Improves awareness of geomagnetic storms and radio blackouts. - Helps users understand how solar activity can affect communication, navigation and technological infrastructure. - Provides an accessible way to explore aurora visibility conditions. - Brings information from NASA and NOAA into one interactive platform. - Supports students, educators and space enthusiasts interested in space science. 3. What is the intended impact? Our intended impact is to improve public awareness and understanding of space weather. Solar activity is not limited to what happens in space; it can influence Earth's technological systems and natural environment. However, scientific space-weather information can be difficult for ordinary users to interpret. AuroraX aims to bridge this gap by transforming scientific measurements into understandable visualisations, alerts and useful insights. Our long-term vision is to encourage curiosity about space science and make space-weather information more accessible to people around the world. 4. What tools, coding languages, hardware and software were used? We developed AuroraX using web technologies and publicly available scientific data services with partially help of AI Programming Languages: - HTML – Website structure. - CSS – Interface design and responsive styling. - JavaScript – Data processing, API integration and interactive functionality. AI used:

-claude-frontend source code Technologies and Services: - NASA DONKI API – Solar flares and coronal mass ejections. - NOAA SWPC – Real-time space-weather measurements and alerts. - Netlify Functions – Backend API handling and data caching. - Netlify – Website hosting and deployment. - CSV – Exporting telemetry data. The project was developed primarily as a software-based platform without requiring specialised physical hardware. 5. How is the project creative and innovative? AuroraX combines multiple scientific data sources into a single interactive space-weather intelligence platform. Instead of simply displaying raw scientific measurements, it connects telemetry, impact assessments, aurora estimation and solar-event monitoring in one place. One of its distinctive features is the Aurora Visibility Estimator, which uses geographical coordinates and geomagnetic latitude to estimate whether current geomagnetic conditions may support aurora visibility. Another innovative aspect is the integration of NASA and NOAA information into an accessible dashboard that connects solar activity with its possible effects on Earth. 6. What factors did the team consider? During development, our team considered several important factors: - Scientific accuracy: Using recognised NASA and NOAA data sources. - Accessibility: Making scientific information understandable to non-experts. - Real-time information: Displaying updated measurements and official alerts. - User experience: Creating an organised and interactive interface. - Reliability: Implementing API handling, caching and fallback data access. - Privacy: Using location access only when the user chooses to share their location. - Transparency: Explaining data sources, calculation methods and the limitations of aurora estimates. Conclusion AuroraX represents our effort to connect space science with everyday understanding. By combining real-time solar telemetry, space-weather impact information, aurora estimation and official solar-event records, we aim to make the dynamic relationship between the Sun and Earth easier to explore.
